messages:
mia (support): FYI got a support ticket from BrightBeam, dedicated pool eu-west-1. P95/99 latency spikes and intermittent 429s started at ~09:00 UTC after their nightly batch. They see sudden token-generation stalls and request-level 429s even though quotas look fine. Logs point to repeated KV cache misses and GPU SM saturation pulses. Can eng-runtime / eng-sre help triage? :eyes:

opsbot: [alert] Tenant brightbeam experienced 429 bursts (count=142) and p99 token latency > 3s between 2026-03-15T09:02:00Z and 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z. Autoscaler bumped slice-count +1 at 09:06Z.

sam (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you paste the pool/slice ids and attach the perf dump? Quick checks: is this a fractional MIG packing case or full-slice? If it's fractional, we often see L3 bandwidth thrash between slices.

mia (support): Pool: eu-west-1-dedicated-42, slice id: slice-7a9d. Customer says they're on 1g. They shared a short log snippet showing repeated KV cache misses: 

```
time=09:03:42 tenant=brightbeam req_id=xx kv_cache_hit=false load_time_ms=42 sm_util=96
time=09:03:43 tenant=brightbeam req_id=xy kv_cache_hit=false load_time_ms=48 sm_util=99
time=09:03:44 tenant=brightbeam req_id=xz kv_cache_hit=false load_time_ms=512 sm_util=29
```

mia (support): Also attached their pod events and top-line metrics (CPU idle, GPU sm spiking).

jordan (eng-sre): Okay. First hypothesis: co-located cohost is causing intermittent PCIe/NVLink congestion or L3 cache invalidation. Steps to repro: run a kernel-bound microbench on neighbor slice and run synthetic inference concurrently to see tail effects. We should capture nvidia-smi dmon and nvprof/perf counters over a 2-3 minute window.

sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. Quick diagnostics to run on the node (can run from debug ssh):

```
# sample commands
sudo apt-get install -y gpustat nvtop
watch -n 0.5 nvidia-smi dmon -s u
# if perf available:
sudo perf record -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 120
# capture nvlink/pcie errors
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,clocks.gr,clocks.mem --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu_util.csv &
```

sam (eng-runtime): Also run our intra-node microbench to saturate memory bandwidth: `python -m tools.synth_load --mode=memband --duration=120 --gpu 0` on suspected neighbor. If tail increases when microbench runs, that's a strong signal.

lina (customer-success): Customer says their batch job is a short burst of many small prompts (seq len ~32) at high qps for 20s windows. They suspect it was fine earlier this week and only began after a parallel nightly pipeline was added.

jordan (eng-sre): That pattern (many short requests) is exactly the worst-case for L3 thrash and KV cache churn. Mitigations we can try immediately: 1) move brightbeam's slice to an isolated node (evict other fractional slices) for a repro window, 2) temporarily change MIG config to larger slice (reduce cohabitation), or 3) enable per-tenant QoS shaping to smooth burst. Which is quickest for support ops?

mia (support): We can request a short maintenance window to isolate. Ops will need the node id and target time. If eng-sre wants to run the microbench we can coordinate.

sam (eng-runtime): I can run the microbench if you isolate. Also need: kube pod logs (full), `/var/log/kern.log`, dmesg, and the runtime trace for the requests (we need tokentrace to see exact stall points). Can you collect these artifacts and upload to the ticket?

mia (support): Will collect and upload. Action items: 1) lina to coordinate with BrightBeam for 30m repro window tonight UTC 22:00-22:30, 2) ops to isolate slice-7a9d onto node node-uf7, 3) eng-runtime (sam) to run microbench and collect nvidia/perf dumps, 4) eng-sre (jordan) to review hardware counters and suggest long-term config.

lina (customer-success): I'll confirm the window. BrightBeam agreed to a short repro test at 22:00 UTC.

opsbot: [info] Autoscaler event: scaled up 1 slice at 09:06Z, reason=burst_autoscale. Recorded metric window attached to ticket.

jordan (eng-sre): If we confirm cohost noise, longer-term options: prefer whole-GPU slices for noisy tenants, add kernel-level pci bandwidth gating (we have a prototype patch), and tune KV cache warmup (increase reuse window for small prompts). For now, isolation should prove the case.

sam (eng-runtime): One more diagnostic: capture per-request kvcache keyset size and hit-rate. If hit-rate collapses under burst, our batching and prefix caching logic may be thrashing. Add `--profiling kvcache` to the runtime config during repro.

mia (support): Noted. I'll attach a checklist to the ticket and mark the thread "repro-scheduled" once ops confirms. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
